keep.quote: Envy comes in two kinds: benign envy pushes you to move up, malicious envy to pull the other down (c07).
At the 1992 Olympics, bronze medallists looked happier than silver: silver thinks of the gold it nearly won, bronze of nearly winning nothing (c08).

Then the national exam, where in most subjects the top grade also goes to the top four per cent, but of everyone in the country who sits it (c01): the same word, "four per cent", meaning a seat in one case and a sea in the other, which is the film's late think-moment without any time skip.
